speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked	the Minister for Defence (a) how much is the Government paying for the extra days of National Day Parade (NDP) rehearsals at the Sports Hub; and (b) whether the Government expects to pay similar amounts for future years when the Sports Hub is chosen as the NDP venue again.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked	the Minister for Defence (a) what is the current estimated total cost for National Day Parade (NDP) 2016 after including the cost of rental for the extra days of rehearsals; and (b) how does this compare to the NDP costs of the previous five years.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When compared to other NDP sites at the Padang and the Marina Bay Floating Platform, the new setting calls for a different format.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, what Members here particularly like and what Singaporeans like, the Red Lions parachuting down into the site will not be possible for obvious safety reasons.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We will also not be able to have a mobile column or aerial displays because we just cannot see them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: However, the new National Stadium also provides advantages for a different type of show, utilising the larger confined space and central pitch as a large stage.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The NDP 2016 Executive Committee, the Exco, is excited about the possibilities that the new setting provides and has been hard at work preparing for NDP 2016 so that all Singaporeans can enjoy it and be proud of it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Another distinct advantage of the new National Stadium, because it has a seating capacity of 55,000, almost twice the number of Singaporeans who can watch it either at the Padang or the Marina Bay Platform, is exactly this: there will be many more Singaporeans who will be able to watch the rehearsals and the NDP physically at the site, compared to the Marina Bay Floating Platform and the Padang.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Both of these have capacities of about 25,000.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In all, in the new site, we expect about 275,000 Singaporeans to be able to watch the National Education shows, the Preview show and NDP 2016 physically at the site.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As with previous NDPs, "live" telecast will also allow Singaporeans to watch the shows at home.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Page: 20 Let me address the questions which have been posed regarding the costs of NDP at the National Stadium, and compare it, as asked, with NDPs held at the Marina Bay Floating Platform or the Padang.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There have been questions asked about itemised cost.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Itemised cost comparisons between the three different sites are sometimes difficult and not meaningful as the venue conditions vary considerably for each site.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, among these factors, the number of "live" spectators in the main venue and surrounding areas, the costs for added security in some sites will be more than the others, and also the collateral impact of opportunity costs on surrounding businesses and retails shops.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Be that as it may, I will still give some figures and some comparisons.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The cost of the show segment, for example, for all three sites is similar, about half of total costs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the cost to build infrastructure varies considerably.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, each time we hold it at the Padang, we have to build all the spectator stands and that costs about 22% of the total cost, as you can well imagine.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But it is negligible at the Marina Bay Floating Platform and the National Stadium because it is already built.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Exco is aware that after the Golden Jubilee NDP and SG50 celebrations, expectations of this year's show, NDP 2016, are high and I think that they have resigned themselves to the fact that comparisons will be inevitable.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: However, I believe that, ultimately, the NDP is a show with Singaporeans, for Singaporeans and by Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The committee will do their best to live up to expectations, but I ask that Singaporeans support the Exco so that they can put up a really good NDP this year for all of us to celebrate together.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first supplementary question is: the Minister mentioned that for NDP 2016, the venue cost would be about 15% of the infrastructure cost, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could he specify in dollar terms, how much would the rental of the Sports Hub cost?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For the second question, Madam, we understand that the agreement between the Government and the Sports Hub allows the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) to use the Sports Hub for 45 days free of charge each year.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My question is: did the Government foresee that it would be holding the NDP at the Sports Hub?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Next, why were only 45 days provided for when we understand that the average number of days needed for the NDP is closer to about 80 days?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Third, is there any dispute resolution mechanism provided for under the public-private partnership between the Government and the Sports Hub over the use of the Hub?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member asked for details relating to the contract.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For 2016, what is the proportion between the cost for rehearsals versus the cost for the actual venue for the actual day itself, as well as the key rehearsals, for example, the 45 days set aside versus the 80 days needed?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Did the Ministry consider doing the rehearsals elsewhere and why were alternative locations not considered to save on the cost?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In other words, they come together when they feel that there is a need to be physically at the stadium.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Whether it is held at the Padang, Floating Platform or the National Stadium, they start fairly early.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In fact, they usually start about seven or eight months before the actual show in various groups, and some of these are held in camps.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But ultimately, to put up a good show, we have to put people together and test it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Whether we could have done or we can do more of it off-site and then come to the venue itself, I leave it to the Exco.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The mandate and the deliverable for them are to put up a good show.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I will pass the suggestion by the Member to them, to see whether they can reduce costs by doing it off-site and they will have to determine whether they can.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The third question is: the Minister mentioned in his speech that public expectations have risen since the SG50 NDP.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In last year's Budget, we were told by the Government that extra expenditure was expected for NDP 2015 because it was the SG50 year.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether it is actually not correct or not justifiable for the Government to proceed on the basis that SG50 is a benchmark for future parades in non-milestone years.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The last question is: the Minister did not quite answer my question about the dispute resolution under the public-private partnership (PPP).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is he able to give a more detailed answer about how disputes will be resolved under the agreement?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I never said that last year's NDP would be used as a benchmark.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member has chosen not to talk about that figure but to move back to her points.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Page: 22 So, let me clarify the answer to the question asked.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have given itemised costs in terms of what it costs for infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member has asked whether we will provide details in the Budget.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member has been in this House for many years and knows that we do not provide those details in the Budget and, if Members ask a question, we will tell you.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: National Day has historically been at the National Stadium for many, many years.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Floating Platform and the Padang were a change for about the last 10 years or so.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But now that it is coming back to the National Stadium, what I am really interested in is that the Minister mentioned that 275,000 people would be able to enjoy it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Would this also mean that there will be more tickets available for things like the previews and so on?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: What is the usual number of people who apply for these tickets because I know there are a lot of disappointed people every year?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have usually many more who apply than can come.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: All I can say is that more than double the number of people will be able to watch it at the National Stadium.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But still, there will be many more who cannot because the numbers go up.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Now that I have given this figure that 275,000 can watch it, I am sure I will get more than double the number of people applying.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: That was in the Parliamentary Question I filed.
